Adopt the distinct massless classical particle action on this segment

$$S_{0,[a,b]}[x,p,e]=\int_a^b\left[p_a x'^a-eC_0(x,p)\right]d\lambda,\qquad C_0=\tfrac12g^{ab}p_ap_b.$$

Select stationary triples on the future shell branch after taking the independent variations: when $m>0$, $p^\sharp$ is future timelike; when $m=0$, require $p\ne0$ and $p^\sharp$ future null. $$I_m[x,p,e]=\int_a^b\left(p_ax'^a-eC_m(x,p)\right)d\lambda.$$

Take independent smooth variations of $p,e$ and fixed-endpoint variations of $x$. Stationarity on the chart segment is equivalent to

$$x'^a=e g^{ab}p_b,\quad p'_a=-\tfrac e2\partial_a g^{bc}p_bp_c,\quad C_m=0.$$

For a covector $p$ and vector $v$ in the canonical coordinates, write $p\cdot v:=\sum_i p_i v^i$. $$S(t,q(t,a))=S_0(a)+\int_0^t[p(u,a)\cdot\dot q(u,a)-H(u,q(u,a),p(u,a))],du$$

derivations.claim: Put $p(t)=S_q(t,q(t))$. From $S_t+H(t,q,S_q)=0$, differentiation with respect to $q$ gives $S_{qt}+H_q+H_pS_{qq}=0$. Since $\dot q=H_p$, the chain rule yields $\dot p=S_{qt}+S_{qq}\dot q=-H_q$. Thus $(q,p)$ satisfies both Hamilton equations.

Implicit differentiation of $C_m(t,q,p_0(t,q,p),p)=0$ gives $H_{p_i}=cC_{p_i}/C_{p_0}=eC_{p_i}$ and $-H_{q^i}=-cC_{q^i}/C_{p_0}=-eC_{q^i}$. Thus $\dot x^0=c=eC_{p_0}$, $\dot x^i=eC_{p_i}$, and $\dot p_i=-eC_{q^i}$. Differentiating $C_m=0$ along the lifted curve makes the $q^i,p_i$ terms cancel and gives $C_{p_0}\dot p_0=-cC_{x^0}$, hence $\dot p_0=-eC_{x^0}$. The inverse projection and complete-integral coordinates from [L2]–[L3] apply only where their Jacobians remain nonsingular. If that projection loses invertibility, the single-valued graph $p=S_q$ used in step 1.1 is no longer supplied; therefore no extension through that point or beyond the actual chart interval follows.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the cotangent/H7/H9 supplier chain. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open time interval, $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ an open spatial chart domain, and $(N,\beta,h)$ smooth temporal-chart data with $N>0$ and $h_{ij}$ positive definite as in [[def-rpm-h-temporal-chart-data]]. Take $m\ge0$ in kg and $c>0$ in m/s. On the future shell define $\kappa(t,q,p)=\sqrt{m^2c^2+h^{ij}(t,q)p_ip_j}$ and the positive-root reduced Hamiltonian $H(t,q,p)=c\bigl(N\kappa-\beta^ip_i\bigr)$ from [[thm-rpm-h-temporal-shell-reduction]]; its domain is $U=I\times T^*\Omega$ for $m>0$, and the open subset with $p\ne0$ for $m=0$. Here $t$ is measured in seconds, $q$ in metres, $p$ in kg m/s, $H$ in joules, and $S$ in joule-seconds. Let $D\subseteq I\times\Omega$ be open and let $S\in C^2(D,\mathbb R)$ (all partial derivatives through order two are continuous) satisfy $S_t+H(t,q,S_q)=0$ wherever $(t,q,S_q)\in U$. If $S$ is the smooth local solution supplied by [[thm-rpm-h-local-hamilton-jacobi]] from an initial exact-graph point in $U$, and $J=[t_1,t_2]\subset I$ with $t_1<t_2$ is an interval on which its characteristic projection remains invertible, let $q:J\to\Omega$ be a $C^1$ characteristic with $\dot q=H_p(t,q,S_q)$. Then $p(t):=S_q(t,q(t))$ satisfies $\dot p=-H_q$, so $(q,p)$ obey Hamilton's equations. The smooth ODE makes this characteristic smooth; by [[thm-rpm-h-temporal-shell-reduction]] these reduced equations are exactly the equations of the future-shell first-order system of [[thm-rpm-h-first-order-action-and-geodesics]]. Under the matching adopted model postulate, this curve is a trajectory of the massive or separate massless model. The conclusion holds only on the chart and local solution interval; it does not continue through a caustic or assert a global HJ solution. It is a conditional mathematical prediction, not a reported observation.

The characteristic graph is restricted to points with $(t,q,S_q(t,q))\in U$. The action $S$ is measured in joule-seconds.

The Lagrangian is **regular** at $(t,q,v)$ when the velocity Hessian $(\partial^2L/\partial v^i\partial v^j)$ is invertible there; regularity gives only a local inverse branch. It is **hyperregular on a declared domain** when $\mathbb F L$ is a diffeomorphism from that entire domain onto an open subset of $\mathbb R\times T^*Q$.

It is **almost regular on a declared domain $\mathcal D_0\subseteq\mathcal D$** when the following are all assumed: $\mathbb F L|_{\mathcal D_0}$ has constant rank; its image $N$ is an embedded submanifold of $\mathbb R\times T^*Q$; its corestriction $\mathcal D_0\to N$ is a surjective submersion (its differential is surjective at every point); and every fibre of that corestriction is connected. These hypotheses are not consequences of singularity alone.

$$T^*Q=\coprod_{q\in Q}T_q^*Q,\qquad \pi:T^*Q\to Q,\quad \pi(q,p)=q,$$

with the canonical smooth structure and induced cotangent charts supplied by the manifold construction in [[def-tautological-one-form-on-a-cotangent-bundle]]. The **tautological one-form** is $\theta_{(q,p)}(\xi)=p(d\pi_{(q,p)}\xi)$, and the **canonical cotangent two-form** is $\omega=-d\theta$. The exact theorem [[thm-the-canonical-cotangent-two-form-is-symplectic]] makes $(T^*Q,\omega)$ a symplectic manifold in the sense of [[def-symplectic-form-and-symplectic-manifold]]. We call this pair the **cotangent phase space** of $Q$.

In an induced chart $(q^1,\ldots,q^n,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$, $\theta=p_i\,dq^i$ and $\omega=dq^i\wedge dp_i$. A mathematical **observable** on this phase space means a smooth function $F:T^*Q\to\mathbb R$; this definition does not assert that a measurement has been performed or that every such function is physically measurable.

For an interpreted particle model, assign coordinates $q^i$ their declared units and assign the conjugate covector components $p_i$ units of action divided by the units of $q^i$. Thus $\theta$ and $\omega$ have action units, conventionally joule-seconds, and a bracket of quantities with units \([F]\) and \([G]\) has units \([F][G]/(\text{action})\). These are dimensional interpretations of the model, not additional mathematical premises. The use of $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$ is exactly the use in the smooth cotangent-bundle suppliers; no full Axiom of Choice is used.

$$C:=\{z\in U:\chi_1(z)=\cdots=\chi_r(z)=0\}$$

when $d\chi_1(z),\ldots,d\chi_r(z)$ are linearly independent at every $z\in C$. The regular-level theorem [[thm-a-regular-level-set-is-an-embedded-submanifold]] then gives $C$ its embedded-submanifold structure and $T_zC=\bigcap_a\ker d\chi_a(z)$. For functions $F,G$ on $U$, write $F\approx G$ when $F|_C=G|_C$; thus $F\approx0$ means that $F$ vanishes on $C$, without requiring it to vanish off $C$.

Given a smooth canonical Hamiltonian $H_c$ on $U$ and multiplier functions $u^a(t)$, the **total generator** is

$$H_T(t,z):=H_c(t,z)+\sum_{a=1}^r u^a(t)\chi_a(z).$$

The functions $u^a$ are independent parameter functions; the definition does not assert that their equations determine them. If $H_c$ is an energy and $\chi_a$ has units \([\chi_a]\), then $u^a$ has units energy divided by \([\chi_a]\), so every term in $H_T$ has the same units. A later constraint, if generated by consistency, is not declared primary by this definition.

Use the signature $(-,+,+,+)$ throughout. In the flat case, **Minkowski spacetime** means the affine model $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ of [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]]: $A$ is an affine space, $\eta$ is a nondegenerate Lorentz form on its four-dimensional displacement space, and $C^+$ selects the future cone. In the curved case, a **background spacetime** means a prescribed smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold $(M,g,N)$ of [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]; the metric and time orientation are fixed data, not dynamical unknowns here. No field equation or completeness assumption is included.

A **massive worldline** on an open interval $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ is a $C^2$ curve $x:I\to M$ with future-directed timelike tangent $T=dx/ds$ at every parameter value. This is the smooth subclass of [[def-gr-timelike-worldline-and-proper-time]]. A **null worldline** is a $C^2$ curve with nonzero future-directed null tangent everywhere. Its tangent has no proper-time normalization: $g(T,T)=0$, so the massive proper-time formula does not apply. In the flat model these are affine curves into $A$ with tangent in the selected future timelike or null cone from [[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]].

An **observer at an event** $p\in M$ is a future unit timelike vector $n\in T_pM$ with $g_p(n,n)=-1$, as in [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]. Its instantaneous rest space is $n^\perp=\{v:g_p(v,n)=0\}$. This is a pointwise vector-space construction; the definition does not assign a clock reading or a moving frame to a lone observer.

An **observer congruence** on an open set $U\subseteq M$ is a smooth field of future unit timelike vectors on $U$, as in [[def-gr-observer-congruence-and-adapted-charts]]; its observer curves are its integral curves. A **tetrad** is a chosen orthonormal frame field, as in [[def-gr-local-frame-and-tetrad-fields]]. A **chart** is a coordinate map; an adapted chart is a chart whose spatial coordinates are constant along the congruence's integral curves. These objects are distinct: a chart need not be inertial, a tetrad need not be coordinate induced, and a congruence is a field of observers rather than a chart or a frame. This distinction agrees with [[def-sr-chart-tetrad-and-congruence-distinction]].

The coordinates and units used later are SI: in an inertial chart $x^0=ct$ and $x^i$ are metres, $t$ is seconds, $c>0$ is metres per second, and proper time is measured in seconds. In a general chart, coordinate components inherit their coordinate units; invariant equations are tensorial. No global inertial chart, global tetrad, or global observer congruence is asserted to exist.

$$p_a=mc\frac{g_{ab}V^b}{s},\qquad s=\sqrt{-g(V,V)}>0.$$

The velocity Hessian is $mc(g_{ab}/s+V_aV_b/s^3)$, has kernel exactly $\mathbb RV$, and rank three. The image consists exactly of the future shell $\Sigma_m^+=\{(x,p)\in T^*M:g_x^{-1}(p,p)=-m^2c^2,\ p^\sharp\text{ future}\}$. Each fibre is a connected positive ray, and the Legendre map is a surjective submersion onto this embedded image. Its energy $p(V)-L$ is zero; the map has no local inverse in the four-velocity direction.

Let $\mathcal V\subset TM$ be an open neighborhood of $\Sigma_c^+$ contained in the future timelike velocity cone. For a massive body trajectory $x:I\to M$ that is $C^2$ and parameterized by proper time $\tau$, with $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ a nonempty open interval, put $U=dx/d\tau$ and require $(x(\tau),U(\tau))\in\Sigma_c^+\subseteq\mathcal V$ for every $\tau\in I$. Specify a smooth map $f:\mathcal V\to TM$ over the bundle projection $\pi:TM\to M$, meaning $\pi(f(p,V))=p$ (equivalently, $f(p,V)\in T_pM$), and require $g_p(V,f(p,V))=0$ for every $(p,V)\in\mathcal V$. $$D_\tau P=f(x,U).$$

The orthogonality condition is part of this model's compatibility assumptions, imposed throughout $\mathcal V$; it preserves $g(U,U)=-c^2$ for constant $m$. Let $M$ be a smooth four-manifold without boundary and let $g$ be a smooth
symmetric covariant $2$-tensor field on $M$ such that $g_p$ is nondegenerate at
every $p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-covariant-two-tensor-field]]). Assume
$\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-smooth-vector-field-as-a-tangent-bundle-section]]).
For this general metric define $\flat_p(v):=g_p(v,\cdot)$,
$\sharp_p:=\flat_p^{-1}$, and
$g_p^{-1}(\alpha,\beta):=g_p(\sharp_p\alpha,\sharp_p\beta)$.
Nondegeneracy makes $\flat_p$ injective and hence invertible between the
four-dimensional tangent space and its dual. In a chart, $g^{ab}$ are the
entries of the inverse matrix of $(g_{ab})$. These definitions agree with
[[def-gr-inverse-metric-and-musical-isomorphisms]] in its Lorentzian scope.
Here and below repeated upper/lower indices are summed over $0,1,2,3$.
This holds in particular
when $(M,g,N)$ is a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and $g$ is
its metric ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]). For smooth local vector fields
$X,Y,Z$ put

$$K(X,Y,Z):=X\bigl(g(Y,Z)\bigr)+Y\bigl(g(Z,X)\bigr)-Z\bigl(g(X,Y)\bigr)+g([X,Y],Z)+g([Z,X],Y)-g([Y,Z],X),$$

with brackets as in [[def-lie-bracket-of-smooth-vector-fields]].

**(a) Existence and formulas.** There is exactly one affine connection
$\nabla$ on $M$ ([[def-affine-connection-on-a-smooth-manifold]]) satisfying

$$2g(\nabla_XY,Z)=K(X,Y,Z)\qquad\text{for all smooth local }X,Y,Z .$$

It is torsion-free and $g$-compatible, so it is a metric-selected connection
for $(M,g)$, meaning torsion-free and satisfying
$Xg(Y,Z)=g(\nabla_XY,Z)+g(Y,\nabla_XZ)$ for smooth local fields
(the conditions of [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]] extended here to
nondegenerate $g$); in every smooth chart its
Christoffel symbols are

$$\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=\tfrac12\,g^{ad}\bigl(\partial_bg_{dc}+\partial_cg_{bd}-\partial_dg_{bc}\bigr),$$

with $g^{ad}$ the inverse-metric components defined above
([[def-christoffel-symbols-of-an-affine-connection]]).

**(b) Uniqueness.** If an affine connection $\nabla'$ on $M$ is torsion-free
and $g$-compatible, then $\nabla'=\nabla$. Consequently the class
$\operatorname{LC}(M,g)$ of metric-selected connections has exactly one
element; it is the **Levi–Civita connection** of $g$.

**(c) Induced derivative on tensor fields.** Let $\nabla^*$ be the dual
connection on $T^*M$ and let the product connection of
[[def-product-connection-on-tensor-and-hom-bundles]] act on
$T^r_sM:=(TM)^{\otimes r}\otimes(T^*M)^{\otimes s}$, for integers $r,s\ge0$,
constructed by [[lem-finite-tensor-products-of-smooth-vector-bundles]]. A
type $(r,s)$ tensor at $p$ is a multilinear map
$(T_p^*M)^r\times(T_pM)^s\to\mathbb R$
([[def-type-r-s-tensor-on-a-finite-dimensional-vector-space]]); a smooth
tensor field is a section with smooth coefficients in each local product
frame. The empty product is the scalar line. Its chart components are
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}=T(dx^{a_1},\ldots,dx^{a_r},\partial_{b_1},\ldots,\partial_{b_s})$,
where $dx^a$ is dual to $\partial_a$. This agrees with
[[def-gr-tensor-fields-and-components]] in the Lorentzian case. Put
$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}:=(\nabla_{\partial_c}T)^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}$.
Then, in every smooth chart, for
every smooth tensor field $T$ of type $(r,s)$,

$$T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s;c}=\partial_cT^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}+\sum_{i=1}^{r}\Gamma^{a_i}{}_{dc}\,T^{a_1\cdots d\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots b_s}-\sum_{j=1}^{s}\Gamma^{d}{}_{b_jc}\,T^{a_1\cdots a_r}{}_{b_1\cdots d\cdots b_s},$$

where the slot marked $d$ replaces the named index; this derivative commutes
with every contraction in the sense of [[def-contraction-of-a-mixed-tensor]],
and it annihilates the metric and the inverse metric:

$$g_{ab;c}=0,\qquad g^{ab}{}_{;c}=0 .$$

The vectors $P$ and $n$ are future timelike, so [F3] gives $g(P,n)<0$ and therefore $E_n=-cg(P,n)>0$. For null $P$, since $g(P,P)=0$, [F2] yields $g(q,q)=g(P,n)^2$, and positivity selects $E_n=c\sqrt{g(q,q)}$.

Under the flat inertial constant-mass hypotheses, [F1] identifies the prescribed force with the derivative of the mechanical momentum, and [F4] supplies the coordinate work relation. The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

They are primitive model parameters; this definition does not derive them from the background field or from another framework.
- The **kinetic four-momentum** is the derived vector $P:=mU$ along $z$, with unit kilogram metre per second.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure, and let $\nabla$ be the metric-selected Levi–Civita connection of [[thm-gr-nondegenerate-levi-civita-and-tensor-derivative]]. Let $U$ and the prescribed external two-form $F$ be as in [[def-rpm-charge-spin-model]], and let the translational motion obey the adopted action law [[post-rpm-external-charge-action]]. For a $C^1$ spin or polarization vector $s$ along the worldline with $g(s,U)=0$, define $G:=g_s/2$ and $K:=F(s,U)=g(s,F^\sharp(U))$. Adopt the transport law

(a) [Components] For a field pair $(E,B)$ of class $C^k$, $k\ge1$, define the
covariant components of the **electromagnetic two-form** $F$ in the chart by
$F_{00}=0$, $F_{0i}:=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}:=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$
($i,j,k\in\{1,2,3\}$) and $F_{ab}:=-F_{ba}$, the index-raised components being
$F^{0i}=E_i/c$, $F^{i0}=-E_i/c$ and $F^{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$. Here
$\epsilon_{ijk}$ is the spatial permutation symbol of
[[def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form]]. Then $F$ is a $C^k$ type-$(0,2)$
tensor field on $U$ in the sense of
[[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]], alternating at every event, and the
components above are exactly its component functions: at $p\in U$ the tensor
$F(p)$ is the bilinear form $F(p)(u,w)=F_{ab}(p)u^aw^b$ on $V$ in the
coordinates $u^a,w^b$ of $u,w$ in $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$. Indeed each $F_{ab}$ is
a finite sum of products of the $C^k$ functions $E_i,B_k$ of the chart
coordinates with the constants $c,\epsilon_{ijk}$, hence a $C^k$ function of
$x(p)$, and the component criterion of
[[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]] applies.

It is distinct from the potential-dependent covector defined in [[lem-rpm-charge-gauge-boundary]].
- The **spin or polarization vector** is a $C^1$ tangent vector field $s(\tau)\in T_{z(\tau)}M$ constrained by $g(s,U)=0$, so it lies in the positive-definite instantaneous rest space $U^\perp$.

Assume Countable Choice for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure supplied by the GR items below. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold with its metric-compatible connection $\nabla$, let $c>0$, and let $z:I\to M$ be a $C^2$ future timelike curve parametrized by proper time $\tau$, with $U=D_\tau z$ and $g(U,U)=-c^2$. Let $F_\tau$ be a continuous alternating two-form along $z$. Define $F^\sharp_\tau$ by
$$g(F^\sharp_\tau(v),w)=F_\tau(w,v).$$
Then $F^\sharp_\tau$ is skew-adjoint with respect to $g$.

For constants $\alpha,a,b\in\mathbb R$, consider the restricted linear transport equations
$$D_\tau U=\alpha F^\sharp(U),\qquad D_\tau s=\alpha\left(aF^\sharp(s)+\frac{b}{c^2}U\,\kappa\right),\qquad \kappa:=g(s,F^\sharp(U)).$$
For every initial $s(\tau_0)$ there is a unique solution on each compact subinterval of $I$. Along any such solution,
$$\frac{d}{d\tau}g(U,s)=\alpha(1-a-b)\kappa.$$
Consequently, the orthogonality constraint $g(U,s)=0$ is preserved when $a+b=1$, and on that constraint $g(s,s)$ is constant. For the coefficient comparison, fix a parameter value $\tau$ and put $n:=U(\tau)/c$. Then $n$ is an observer at $z(\tau)$ and its rest space is the three-dimensional positive-definite subspace $E_\tau:=n^\perp=U(\tau)^\perp$ (the observer and projection conventions are those of [[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]] and [[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]]). Choose an orientation of $E_\tau$ and a positively oriented orthonormal basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$; set $e_0:=n$. For $v\in E_\tau$, write $\mathbf v=(g(v,e_1),g(v,e_2),g(v,e_3))$, use $(\mathbf u\times\mathbf v)_i=\epsilon_{ijk}u_jv_k$, and define $\mathbf B$ by $F_{ij}:=F(e_i,e_j)=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$. Let $P_U(v):=v+g(U,v)U/c^2$, the projection onto $E_\tau$. The rest-space matching condition means the pointwise equality
$$\bigl(P_U(D_\tau s)\bigr)^i=\alpha G\,(\mathbf s\times\mathbf B)_i\qquad(i=1,2,3)$$
for every $\mathbf s,\mathbf B$, when $s(\tau)\in E_\tau$. Thus it compares spatial components of the covariant derivative at the event, not the derivative of components in an unspecified moving tetrad. For $\alpha\ne0$, if the coefficients both preserve $g(U,s)=0$ for every initially orthogonal datum and every allowed alternating field and satisfy this matching condition, then $a=G$ and $b=1-G$. Conversely, these coefficients satisfy both requirements. This uniqueness is only within the displayed two-term ansatz; no uniqueness among all covariant spin-transport laws is asserted. If $\alpha=0$, the rest-space matching condition does not identify $a$ or $b$.

Adopt the pole-dipole evolution equations
$$D_\tau p^a=-\frac12 R^a{}_{bcd}U^bS^{cd},\qquad D_\tau S^{ab}=p^aU^b-p^bU^a.$$
A spin-supplementary condition (SSC) is an additional equation $S^{ab}n_b=0$ for a specified future unit timelike field $n$ along $z$; this postulate does not select one SSC, and $p$ is an independently evolved moment rather than a primitive assumption $p=mU$.

Conversely, on the open state region where $p$ and $W$ are future timelike and $K$ is invertible, the normalized formula for $U$ in (2), together with (1), defines a smooth local ODE. A solution initialized with $C=0$ preserves $C=0$. While it remains in that admissible region, $\mu$ and $S_{ab}S^{ab}/2$ are constant. If $S=0$, then $p=(\mu/c)U$, $D_\tau p=0$, and $D_\tau U=0$. These are local statements; no continuation past loss of invertibility of $K$ or timelikeness of $W$ is asserted. Equations (1) are hypotheses of this mathematical lemma, not a physical derivation of a stress-energy moment model.
**(b) Local curved-body moments.** Let $z\in M$ and let $U_0$ be a convex normal neighborhood containing $z$.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold and let
$p\in M$ ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]).

**(a) Observers.** An **observer at $p$** is a tangent vector
$n\in T_pM$ such that $g_p(n,n)=-1$ and $n$ is future-directed in the sense of
[[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], that is, $g_p(n,N_p)<0$. Because
$g_p(n,n)=-1\neq0$, an observer is timelike and in particular nonzero
([[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]). Observers at $p$ exist:
the vector $N_p$ is timelike, and
$n:=N_p/\sqrt{-g_p(N_p,N_p)}$ satisfies $g_p(n,n)=-1$ and
$g_p(n,N_p)=-\sqrt{-g_p(N_p,N_p)}<0$, where the square root is the
nonnegative root of [[def-rational-power]]; then $-n$ is a unit timelike
vector with $g_p(-n,N_p)>0$, so it is not an observer, and the two vectors
$n,-n$ point in opposite time directions.

**(b) Rest space.** For an observer $n$ at $p$, the **rest space** of $n$ is
the $g_p$-orthogonal complement of the line $\mathbb Rn$,

$$n^{\perp}=\{v\in T_pM: g_p(v,n)=0\},$$

in the sense of [[def-lorentz-orthogonality-and-orthogonal-complement]]. It is
a linear subspace of $T_pM$. The further facts that $\dim n^{\perp}=3$ and
that the restriction of $g_p$ to $n^{\perp}$ is positive definite are proved
in [[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]]; they are consequences, not
part of the definition.

**(c) Spatial projection.** The **spatial projection** of the observer $n$ is
the map

$$h_n:T_pM\longrightarrow T_pM,\qquad h_n(v):=v+g_p(n,v)\,n .$$

The map is linear because $g_p$ is bilinear, its image is contained in
$n^{\perp}$, and it fixes $n^{\perp}$ pointwise; that it is the
$g_p$-orthogonal projection onto $n^{\perp}$ with kernel $\mathbb Rn$ is
proved in [[lem-gr-observer-projection-decomposition]].

**(d) Scope.** An observer at $p$ is a single tangent vector. It is not an
ordered basis or frame of $T_pM$, not a chart, not a field of observers such as
the congruences defined later on this page, and not a curve or a worldline: no
parametrized curve, clock reading, proper time or measurement is attached to
$n$ by this definition. The physical reading of an observer as the direction
of an ideal clock's worldline, and the measurement interpretation of the
observer-relative quantities introduced later on this page, belong to the
physical postulates and unit conventions of the framework and are not asserted
here.

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold, let

([[def-gr-observer-and-rest-space]]). Write $h:=h_n$,

Use the charged/spinning body-model conventions of the now-authored batch-24 carrier [[def-rpm-charge-spin-model]]: a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature $(-+++)$, coordinates $x^0=ct$ in metres, $c>0$, and a $C^2$ future timelike representative curve $z:I\to M$ parametrized by proper time $\tau$ in seconds, with $U=dz/d\tau$ and $g(U,U)=-c^2$. The actual supplier defines these quantities and the SI electromagnetic-tensor convention used here. Assume Countable Choice for the GR smooth-structure, convex-normal and parallel-transport suppliers used below.

**(a) Flat isolated-body moments.** Choose an inertial frame $(o;e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ and its chart $x:A\to\mathbb R^4$ as in [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]], with the SI coordinate convention $x^0=ct$ and $x^i$ in metres of [[def-rpm-charge-spin-model]]. Thus $e_0$ is future unit timelike and $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ is the positively oriented orthonormal spatial basis. Let $T$ be a $C^\infty$ symmetric type-$(2,0)$ tensor field on the affine Minkowski spacetime $A$, whose chart components $T^{ab}$ are the model stress-energy densities with units $\mathrm J\,\mathrm m^{-3}$ and have spatially compact support on every finite time slab. At a fixed time $t$, the spatial slice has coordinates $\mathbf x=(x^1,x^2,x^3)\in\mathbb R^3$ and Lebesgue measure $d^3x$; define
$$p^a(t):=\frac1c\int_{\mathbb R^3}T^{0a}(ct,\mathbf x)\,d^3x,$$
and, for a representative point $z(t)$ on that time slice, define
$$S_z^{ab}(t):=\frac1c\int_{\mathbb R^3}\left((x-z(t))^aT^{0b}(ct,\mathbf x)-(x-z(t))^bT^{0a}(ct,\mathbf x)\right)d^3x.$$
Here $(x-z(t))^0=0$ on the chosen slice, $p$ has units $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$, and $S_z$ has units $\mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-1}}$. These are definitions of moments; no conservation is asserted by clause (a).

**(b) Local curved-body moments.** Let $z\in M$ and let $U_0$ be a convex normal neighborhood containing $z$. Let $\Sigma\subset U_0$ be a $C^1$ embedded spacelike hypersurface through $z$: each tangent space $T_x\Sigma$ is three-dimensional and the restriction of $g_x$ to it is positive definite. Let $n_x$ be its continuous future unit normal, so $g_x(n_x,n_x)=-1$ and $g_x(n_x,w)=0$ for every $w\in T_x\Sigma$, and let $d\Sigma$ be the positive volume measure induced by $g|_{T\Sigma}$. Let $T$ be a smooth symmetric type-$(2,0)$ tensor field on $U_0$; only its restriction $T|_\Sigma$ is used. With $(n_x)_b:=g_{bc}(x)n_x^c$, define
$$\operatorname{supp}_\Sigma(T|_\Sigma):=\overline{\{x\in\Sigma:T_x\ne0\}}^{\,\Sigma}.$$
Assume this restricted support is a compact subset of $U_0$ and that all displayed integrands are absolutely integrable with respect to $d\Sigma$. For every $x\in\Sigma$, let $v(x):=\exp_z^{-1}(x)\in T_zM$ be the unique joining position vector supplied by [[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]] and [[thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map]]. Let $H_{x\to z}:T_xM\to T_zM$ be parallel transport along that unique geodesic, with existence, uniqueness and metric preservation as in [[lem-gr-parallel-transport-and-geodesic-speed]]. Define $T^\sharp(n_x)^a:=T^{ab}(x)(n_x)_b$ and
$$p_z:=\frac1c\int_\Sigma H_{x\to z}\!\left(-T^\sharp(n_x)\right)d\Sigma,\qquad S_z:=\frac1c\int_\Sigma v(x)\wedge H_{x\to z}\!\left(-T^\sharp(n_x)\right)d\Sigma,$$
where $(v\wedge w)^{ab}:=v^aw^b-v^bw^a$ and the finite-dimensional vector and tensor integrals are taken componentwise in any basis of $T_zM$. The resulting $p_z$ and $S_z$ are a vector and an antisymmetric tensor at $z$; their units are $\mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-1}}$ and $\mathrm{kg\,m^2\,s^{-1}}$. “Support on $\Sigma$” here means only compact support of the restriction $T|_\Sigma$; it does not assert that the ambient smooth field $T$ has spacetime support contained in $\Sigma$.

Restrict [[def-rpm-charge-spin-model]] to its flat affine Minkowski branch, with signature $(-,+,+,+)$, proper time $\tau$ in seconds, future four-velocity $U=dx/d\tau$ satisfying $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$, constant primitive $m>0$ in kilograms and nonzero charge $q\in\mathbb R$ in coulombs. Let the prescribed external electromagnetic two-form $F$ be $C^2$ on an open neighborhood of the worldline; use the component convention $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$ of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]]. Let $a:=dU/d\tau$ and

$$\alpha:=q/m,\qquad \tau_e:=\frac{q^2}{6\pi\epsilon_0mc^3}>0,\qquad f_0^a:=\alpha F^a{}_bU^b,$$

where $\epsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ follows [[def-em-si-conventions]]. Adopt the flat LAD effective equation

$$a^a=f_0^a+\tau_e\left(\frac{da^a}{d\tau}-\frac{\eta_{bc}a^ba^c}{c^2}U^a\right).$$

The derivative is the ordinary derivative in an inertial affine chart. Its dimensions are consistent: $a$ and $f_0$ are accelerations, the parenthesized term has acceleration per second, and $\tau_e$ is a time. This is an adopted effective model equation for sufficiently regular curves (at least $C^3$); it is not asserted to be an exact law of nature, a point-source Maxwell construction, or a globally well-posed dynamics. In particular, no existence, uniqueness, stability, or empirical claim is part of this postulate.

Use of the equation as a reduced physical approximation carries the source qualification that radiation reaction be small relative to the applied Lorentz force in the particle's instantaneous rest frame (the inertial frame momentarily comoving with $U$). This postulate neither asserts that condition for arbitrary $F$ nor supplies a numerical threshold; the qualification is not used to deduce the local ODE results or the force-free counterexample.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$ and let $(M^{2n},\omega)$ be a smooth symplectic manifold. A finite family of smooth functions $\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_r$ defined on an open neighborhood $U\subseteq M$ is a **regular primary constraint family** on

$$C:=\{z\in U:\chi_1(z)=\cdots=\chi_r(z)=0\}$$

when $d\chi_1(z),\ldots,d\chi_r(z)$ are linearly independent at every $z\in C$. The regular-level theorem [[thm-a-regular-level-set-is-an-embedded-submanifold]] then gives $C$ its embedded-submanifold structure and $T_zC=\bigcap_a\ker d\chi_a(z)$. For functions $F,G$ on $U$, write $F\approx G$ when $F|_C=G|_C$; thus $F\approx0$ means that $F$ vanishes on $C$, without requiring it to vanish off $C$.

Given a smooth canonical Hamiltonian $H_c$ on $U$ and multiplier functions $u^a(t)$, the **total generator** is

$$H_T(t,z):=H_c(t,z)+\sum_{a=1}^r u^a(t)\chi_a(z).$$

The functions $u^a$ are independent parameter functions; the definition does not assert that their equations determine them. If $H_c$ is an energy and $\chi_a$ has units $[\chi_a]$, then $u^a$ has units energy divided by $[\chi_a]$, so every term in $H_T$ has the same units. A later constraint, if generated by consistency, is not declared primary by this definition.

Let $Q$ be a finite-dimensional smooth manifold as in [[def-rpm-h-cotangent-phase-space]], and write its cotangent phase space in induced coordinates $(q^i,p_i)$. With $\omega=dq^i\wedge dp_i$, define $X_H$ by $\iota_{X_H}\omega=dH$ and define the Poisson bracket by $\{F,G\}:=X_G(F)$. Then

$$X_H=\frac{\partial H}{\partial p_i}\frac{\partial}{\partial q^i}-\frac{\partial H}{\partial q^i}\frac{\partial}{\partial p_i},\qquad \{F,G\}=F_{q^i}G_{p_i}-F_{p_i}G_{q^i}.$$

The bracket is coordinate independent and makes smooth functions a Poisson algebra. If $H_t$ is smooth on an open time-dependent domain $D\subset\mathbb R\times T^*Q$, each solution of $\dot z=X_{H_t}(z)$ has local uniqueness and smooth dependence on initial data and parameters; on its actual interval,

$$\frac{d}{dt}F(t,z(t))=\partial_tF+\{F,H_t\}.$$

No completeness or global flow is asserted. If $H$ is smooth, each local time-$t$ flow map preserves ω.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For every point $p$ of a $2n$-dimensional
symplectic manifold $(M,\omega)$, there are coordinates
$(q^1,\ldots,q^n,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$ centred at $p$ in which

$$\omega=\sum_{i=1}^n dq^i\wedge dp_i.$$

Let $(O,\mathcal L)$ be a time-dependent Lagrangian chart over $[a,b]\times U$ in the sense of
[[def-cm-time-dependent-lagrangian-and-action]] and let $q:[a,b]\to U$ be a $C^2$ admissible curve.
Then $q$ is stationary for the action $S$ if and only if

$$E_{\mathcal L}(q)(t)=0\qquad\text{for every }t\in[a,b].$$

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$: every sequence of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $Q$ be a finite-dimensional, Hausdorff, second-countable smooth manifold without boundary, of dimension $n$. Its cotangent bundle is

$$T^*Q=\coprod_{q\in Q}T_q^*Q,\qquad \pi:T^*Q\to Q,\quad \pi(q,p)=q,$$

with the canonical smooth structure and induced cotangent charts supplied by the manifold construction in [[def-tautological-one-form-on-a-cotangent-bundle]]. The **tautological one-form** is $\theta_{(q,p)}(\xi)=p(d\pi_{(q,p)}\xi)$, and the **canonical cotangent two-form** is $\omega=-d\theta$. The exact theorem [[thm-the-canonical-cotangent-two-form-is-symplectic]] makes $(T^*Q,\omega)$ a symplectic manifold in the sense of [[def-symplectic-form-and-symplectic-manifold]]. We call this pair the **cotangent phase space** of $Q$.

In an induced chart $(q^1,\ldots,q^n,p_1,\ldots,p_n)$, $\theta=p_i\,dq^i$ and $\omega=dq^i\wedge dp_i$. A mathematical **observable** on this phase space means a smooth function $F:T^*Q\to\mathbb R$; this definition does not assert that a measurement has been performed or that every such function is physically measurable.

For an interpreted particle model, assign coordinates $q^i$ their declared units and assign the conjugate covector components $p_i$ units of action divided by the units of $q^i$. Thus $\theta$ and $\omega$ have action units, conventionally joule-seconds, and a bracket of quantities with units $[F]$ and $[G]$ has units $[F][G]/(\text{action})$. These are dimensional interpretations of the model, not additional mathematical premises. The use of $\mathrm{AC}_{\omega}$ is exactly the use in the smooth cotangent-bundle suppliers; no full Axiom of Choice is used.

An **oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space** is a quadruple
$(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ with the following data. In this notation $V$ includes its
specified orientation; forgetting that orientation gives only the underlying
real vector space, not the full datum $V$ of the model.

1. A nonempty affine space $A$ over a $4$-dimensional real vector space $V$,
   with action $(p,v)\mapsto p+v$ and displacement $q-p\in V$
   ([[def-affine-space-and-displacement]]). In particular $V$ is a real vector
   space of dimension $4$.
2. A Lorentz form $\eta$ on $V$, i.e. a nondegenerate symmetric bilinear form of
   inertia $(3,1,0)$ ([[def-lorentz-form-and-inertia]]). Its associated quadratic
   form is $q(v)=\eta(v,v)$.
3. An **orientation** of $V$: a positive ray of the determinant line
   $\Lambda^4V$, fixed once and for all
   ([[def-determinant-line-orientation-of-a-finite-dimensional-real-vector-space]]).
4. A **time orientation** $C^+$ of $(V,\eta)$: one of the two connected
   components of the timelike set $T=\{v\in V:\eta(v,v)<0\}$, the other being
   $C^-:=T\setminus C^+$ ([[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]]).

The following terminology is attached to such a quadruple.

- The elements $p$ of $A$ are the **events**; for events $p,q$ the vector
  $q-p\in V$ is the **displacement from $p$ to $q$**.
- The **interval** of $p,q\in A$ is the real number
  $I(p,q):=\eta(q-p,q-p)=q(q-p)$.
- Events $p,q$ are **timelike**, **null**, **spacelike** or **causally
  related** when the displacement $q-p$ is timelike, null, spacelike or causal
  in the sense of [[def-causal-classification-of-lorentz-vectors]]; they are
  **future-related** when $q-p$ is future causal and **past-related** when
  $q-p$ is past causal in the sense of
  [[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]].

**No point of $A$ is distinguished.** For every $v\in V$ the translation
$\tau_v:A\to A$, $\tau_v(p):=p+v$, is a bijection, since it is inverse to
$\tau_{-v}$: $\tau_{-v}(\tau_v(p))=(p+v)+(-v)=p+(v-v)=p$ and symmetrically, by
the affine action axioms ([[def-affine-space-and-displacement]]). Displacements
are translation invariant, $\tau_v(q)-\tau_v(p)=q-p$, so every $\tau_v$ preserves
the interval, the causal classification of every ordered pair, and the sets
$C^+$, $C^-$ (which are subsets of $V$, independent of the point of $A$); it
changes only the labelling of points. The mathematical structure of the model is
exactly the quadruple $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$; no derived physical quantity (proper
time, four-velocity, momentum, energy, charge or any field) is part of this
definition, and all later structure of the framework (frames, charts, tensor
fields, worldlines) is built on this model.

**Well-definedness.** The affine-space definition supplies the action and the
unique displacements; the Lorentz-form definition supplies $\eta$ and its
inertia; the determinant-line definition supplies orientations; and the two
components of $T$ between which the time-orientation definition chooses exist by
the components lemma recorded in the well-definedness clause of
[[def-time-orientation-and-future-causal-sets]], which is also what makes the
names future and past causal in item 4 well defined.

Let $Q$ be a finite-dimensional smooth manifold as in [[def-rpm-h-cotangent-phase-space]], and write its cotangent phase space in induced coordinates $(q^i,p_i)$. With $\omega=dq^i\wedge dp_i$, define $X_H$ by $\iota_{X_H}\omega=dH$ and define the Poisson bracket by $\{F,G\}:=X_G(F)$. Then

$$X_H=\frac{\partial H}{\partial p_i}\frac{\partial}{\partial q^i}-\frac{\partial H}{\partial q^i}\frac{\partial}{\partial p_i},\qquad \{F,G\}=F_{q^i}G_{p_i}-F_{p_i}G_{q^i}.$$

The bracket is coordinate independent and makes smooth functions a Poisson algebra. If $H_t$ is smooth on an open time-dependent domain $D\subset\mathbb R\times T^*Q$, each solution of $\dot z=X_{H_t}(z)$ has local uniqueness and smooth dependence on initial data and parameters; on its actual interval,

$$\frac{d}{dt}F(t,z(t))=\partial_tF+\{F,H_t\}.$$

No completeness or global flow is asserted. If $H$ is smooth, each local time-$t$ flow map preserves ω.

Let $(P^{2n},\omega)$ be symplectic, and let $N=\{\chi_1=\cdots=\chi_r=0\}$ be a regular embedded level surface with $\{\chi_a,\chi_b\}=0$ on $N$. Then $\ker(\omega|_N)$ is exactly the rank-$r$ distribution spanned by the restricted Hamiltonian vector fields $X_{\chi_a}$. This distribution is involutive. Around every point of $N$, its leaves admit smooth Frobenius coordinates $(s^1,\ldots,s^r,y^1,\ldots,y^{2n-2r})$, and the local leaf space has a unique smooth closed nondegenerate two-form $\omega_{\mathrm{red}}$ whose pullback is $\omega|_N$. Thus regular first-class constraints yield a local symplectic quotient. No global orbit-space regularity follows from these hypotheses.

Let $F:M^m\to N^n$ be smooth, let $q\in N$ be a regular value, and assume
$F^{-1}(q)$ is nonempty. Then $F^{-1}(q)$ is an embedded submanifold of
codimension $n$. Equivalently, it has dimension $m-n$.

Define $C_m(x,p)=	frac12(-p_0^2+|\mathbf p|^2+m^2c^2)$. Solving $C_m=0$ on the future branch gives $p_0=-P^0$ with $P^0=\sqrt{m^2c^2+|\mathbf p|^2}>0$. For $m>0$ work on the full cotangent space; for $m=0$ work on its open subset $U_0=\{(x,p):p
e0\}$. On the zero level in these domains, the vertical differential is $d_pC_m=p^\sharp
e0$: for $m>0$ the shell equation makes $p$ timelike, and for $m=0$ nondegeneracy of $g^{-1}$ and $p
e0$ give $p^\sharp
e0$. Hence [F5] makes the zero level in the stated domain an embedded hypersurface, and $\Sigma_m^+$ is its open future branch. The single constraint is first class because $\{C_m,C_m\}=0$ by skew-symmetry of the canonical Poisson bracket. Thus the regular embedded-level and first-class hypotheses of [F4] hold. Now $y=x^0/P^0$ and $a^i=x^i-(P^i/P^0)x^0$ are smooth shell coordinates, with inverse $x^0=yP^0, x^i=a^i+yP^i$. These formulas prove a diffeomorphism $\Sigma_m^+\cong\mathbb R_y	imes B_m$.

Since the constraint depends only on $p$, [F3] gives its characteristic field $X_C=P^a\partial_{x^a}$; [F4] identifies this direction with the characteristic leaves used for reduction. The flow sends $y\mapsto y+\alpha$ while fixing $a,p$. Hence two points are in the same full orbit exactly when their $a,p$ labels agree, and the quotient map is the product projection to $B_m$.

In shell coordinates $x^0=yP^0, x^i=a^i+yP^i$, so $dx^0=P^0\,dy+y\,dP^0$ and $dx^i=da^i+P^i\,dy+y\,dP^i$. Since $p_0=-P^0$, expanding the canonical form gives $$\omega=da^i\wedge dp_i+dy\wedge(P^i dp_i-P^0dP^0)+y\,dP^i\wedge dp_i.$$ Differentiating $(P^0)^2=m^2c^2+|\mathbf p|^2$ gives $P^0dP^0=P^i dp_i$, so the (dy)-term vanishes. The matrix $\partial P^i/\partial p_j=\delta^{ij}$ is symmetric, so $dP^i\wedge dp_i=0$. The restricted form is therefore the pullback of $da^i\wedge dp_i$, which is nondegenerate on $B_m$.

The spaces $\mathbb R^3$ and $\mathbb R^3\setminus\{0\}$ are Hausdorff second-countable manifolds; their product with $\mathbb R^3_a$ has the same properties. Product projection is a smooth submersion with global section $y=0$, establishing the asserted global quotient directly.
Along every orbit $x^0(\alpha)=x^0(0)+\alpha P^0$, with $P^0>0$, so each level $x^0=ct$ is attained at the unique parameter $\alpha=(ct-x^0(0))/P^0$.
